methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Standard Subsea is a seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Christopher Amidon, having raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a private comparables universe of three peers (Clippership, NetworkOcean, and Albacore) in the same sector, with no public company benchmarks available for direct cross-reference.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using the $10M in total capital raised as a proxy for current implied value, a 2.5x step-up multiplier—standard for progression from seed to Series A—yields a $25M valuation. This reflects typical venture-stage advancement economics within frontier tech infrastructure subsectors.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, with a median point of $25M. The single-method approach and absence of public comparables or revenue-based metrics represent material limitations. Key uncertainties include the actual post-money valuation from the most recent round (which would refine the base), comparable multiples from the three private peers, and revenue or forward-looking metrics that might support alternative approaches. Additional data on burn rate, market sizing, and peer transaction multiples would strengthen conviction in this range.
